lesson.title: The -ité & -ance Bridges
lesson.subtitle: English -ity becomes -ité, -ance/-ence stays whole — and every single one takes la

hook.title: Two More Floors of the Feminine Warehouse
hook.content: In Topic 2 you unlocked thousands of feminine nouns ending in -ion. Today you add two more massive floors to that same building: English words ending in -ity (university, possibility, liberty, reality, quality) swap -ity for -ité (l'université, la possibilité, la liberté, la réalité, la qualité), and English words ending in -ance or -ence (difference, importance, experience, patience, chance) cross into French with the exact same spelling and a nasal vowel!

footnotes.title: Why -ité always wears an acute accent
footnotes.content: Latin abstract nouns in -itātem lost their final syllable in French, leaving a crisp stressed /e/ at the end: université, liberté. That acute accent é is the scar of Latin -tātem.

pattern.title: The Feminine Gender Decoder: -ion, -ité, -ance, -ence
pattern.content: Never memorize gender word by word when the suffix already announces it. Whenever a noun ends in -ion, -ité, -ance, or -ence, it belongs to the feminine squad: la liberté, la différence, l'université, l'importance. And when you replace any of them with 'it', the pronoun is la, walking left before the verb.
pattern.linguist_note: Latin -itās, -antia, and -entia were all feminine abstract suffixes in Rome; French and English inherited the whole set intact.
pattern.trap_note: The shortcut your mind will offer: treating -ance/-ence words like English pronunciation (/əns/). In French, both -ance and -ence share the exact same open nasal vowel /ɑ̃s/: la différence and l'importance rhyme!

summary.takeaway: Four endings (-ion, -ité, -ance, -ence) hand you thousands of feminine nouns without a single flashcard.

université.etymology_derivation: -ity → -ité, and every -ité is feminine. The accent on the é marks the final syllable English swallows.

possibilité.etymology_derivation: Latin possibilitas. The -ty words all convert: ability, activity, university…

liberté.etymology_derivation: liberté/liberty — the Norman doublet in -ité form: same Latin liber, two carriers.

différence.etymology_derivation: Latin differentia. The -ance/-ence endings convert whole and are always feminine.

importance.etymology_derivation: in- + portare 'to carry in' — what gets carried in matters.

expérience.etymology_derivation: Also means 'scientific experiment' in a lab.

chance.etymology_derivation: Late Latin cadentia 'the falling of dice' (doublet of cadence).

ite.name: The -ité Bridge
ite.phonetic_rule: English final -ity becomes stressed final -ité /ite/ — the é marks the syllable English swallows.
ite.historical_linguistics: Latin -itās survives in English -ity and French -ité; both are bookish layers grafted onto the everyday vocabulary, which is why they convert with no sound loss.
ite.philological_note: All -ité nouns are feminine (la possibilité, la liberté).
ite.literature_source: Pope (1952); Brunot, Histoire de la langue française.
